lines.english: “I'm gonna piss myself...”

lines.japanese: 俺は追いこまれていた。
lines.english: I was cornered.

lines.japanese: なんでだ。なんで便所がねえんだ。
lines.english: Why? Why the hell wasn't there a bathroom?

lines.japanese: 正しく言えば、女便所ばっかで男便所がねえ。
lines.english: More precisely, there were women's rooms everywhere and not one men's room.

lines.japanese: 「ケンカ売ってんのかこの建物。その辺にブチ撒けンぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “This building got a problem with me? I'll piss all over the floor, asshole.”

lines.japanese: メットに作業着という泥臭いいでたちの俺にとって、華の女子校という場所はアウェーだった。
lines.english: As a blue-collar guy in a hard hat and work clothes, I was deep in enemy territory at this glamorous girls' school.

lines.japanese: 俺はちょっと前まで、小遣い稼ぎに軽く便利屋の真似事をしていた。
lines.english: Until a little while ago, I'd done some light handyman work to earn pocket money.

lines.japanese: クレープ屋のパルさんを仲介に、人手不足の個人や事業主からちょろっとヘルプ業務を請け負うってカンジで。
lines.english: Paru at the crêpe stand acted as my go-between, and I'd take little jobs helping out individuals or business owners who were short on hands.

lines.japanese: だけど、ちょっと思うところあって、地に足の付いた生活──いわゆる就職ってやつをすることに決めたから、すでにもうそっちの稼業からは手を引いていた。
lines.english: But after thinking some things over, I’d decided to settle into a steady life—get a regular job, in other words. So I’d already quit that line of work.

lines.japanese: 思うところってのは、まあ、いろいろだよ。だから、社会の一員としての責任だとか、自分の抱えてる病気のことだとか、あと……その、なんだ、あー、オンナ？
lines.english: What things had I thought over? A bunch. My responsibility as a member of society, the illness I had to live with, and... you know. Uh, a woman?

lines.japanese: あああ、もう、うっせえ言わせんなボケ。なんだっていいだろ、ほっとけよ。いくら日ごろは硬派な俺だって、ときには人並みにレンアイぐらいすんだよ。
lines.english: Aaargh, shut up and don't make me say it, dumbass. What do you care? Leave me alone. I might be a hard-ass most of the time, but even I can fall in love like a normal person once in a while.

lines.japanese: とにかく、そんなよーなアレやコレやで、俺はもう便利屋をスパッと卒業してたの。
lines.english: Anyway, for those reasons and others, I'd made a clean break from the handyman business.

lines.japanese: けど今回、むかし世話になった電気工事のおっちゃんからどうしても人手が足りないって泣きつかれて、一日かぎりの成田工務店復活と相成ったわけ。俺はこう見えて、義理人情を重んじる男の子なんだ。
lines.english: But this electrician who'd helped me out before begged me to come because he was desperately shorthanded. And so Narita Construction was reuniting for one day only. I may not look it, but I'm a boy who honors his debts and the ties between people.

lines.japanese: しかし、まさかよりによって現場がここ、蒼穹女学院──つまり鳴のガッコーだったとは。
lines.english: Of all places, though, the job had to be here at Azure Sky Girls' Academy—in other words, Naru's school.

lines.japanese: くそっ、こんなところ、あいつにだけは見られたくない。
lines.english: Shit. She was the one person I didn't want seeing me here.

lines.japanese: 俺はそれなりの決意と覚悟をもって便利屋を畳んだし、その件に関してやつに誇らしく語ったりもした（そりゃあ晴れ晴れしい人生の再出発だからな）。
lines.english: I'd shut down the handyman business with a fair amount of resolve and determination, and I'd even bragged to her about it. (It was the bright, beautiful restart of my life, after all.)

lines.japanese: だから一日限りとはいえ、今さら後戻りしたなんて思われたくない。俺はこう見えて、意地や面子を重んじる男の子なんだ。
lines.english: So even if this was just for one day, I didn't want her thinking I'd gone backward. I may not look it, but I'm a boy with pride and a reputation to uphold.

lines.japanese: 俺は後ろ頭をがしがし掻いた。悠長にうろうろしてる場合じゃない。
lines.english: I scratched hard at the back of my head. This was no time to wander around.

lines.japanese: さっさと出すもん出して、視聴覚室で作業してるおっちゃんのとこへ戻ろう。
lines.english: I’d take a piss and get back to the old guy working in the audiovisual room.

lines.japanese: お、丁度いいところに、向こうから乳くせぇガクセーが二匹やってくるじゃないか。
lines.english: Oh, perfect. Two baby-faced students were coming this way.

lines.japanese: おし、手っ取りばやくあいつらに聞いてみよう。
lines.english: All right. I'd save time and ask them.

lines.japanese: 「あースンマセン、男子便所ってどこげえええっ」
lines.english: “Uh, excuse me. Where's the men's roooaargh?!”

lines.japanese: しかし俺の問いかけは、半ばで悲鳴のような呻き声に変わった。
lines.english: But halfway through, my question turned into a groan like a scream.

lines.japanese: 「えええ！　うーっそ隼人君じゃん！」
lines.english: “What?! No way, it's Hayato!”

lines.japanese: 「えええええ？　なななななんで？　なんでなんで？」
lines.english: “Whaaaat? Wh-wh-wh-why? Why, why?”

lines.japanese: 作業着姿の電気業者こと成田隼人を目の当たりにして、にわかに騒然とする小娘たち。
lines.english: The sight of Hayato Narita, electrical contractor in work clothes, sent the little girls into an uproar.

lines.japanese: 香田亜衣と鳳鳴──前者はまだいいとして、後者はまさにいま俺の会いたくない相手そのものじゃねえか。
lines.english: Ai Kouda and Naru Ohtori. The former was one thing; the latter was the exact person I didn't want to meet right now.

lines.japanese: いや、だからアレだ、つまり鳴ってのはその……さっき言ったアレだアレ。あのほら、だからアレだよ。いわゆる俺のアレだよ。うるせえな分かんだろテメエ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ。
lines.english: See, Naru was... the thing I mentioned before. You know, that thing. That. You know what I'm talking about. My thing. Shut the fuck up, you know what I mean. I'll kill you, asshole.

lines.japanese: 「うっわ！　なになに、どゆこと隼人君？　何なんそのカッコ！」
lines.english: “Whoa! Wait, what is this, Hayato? What's with that outfit?!”

lines.japanese: 思わず逃げようかとも思ったが、凄まじいテンションの亜衣に袖を掴まれた。
lines.english: For a moment I thought about running, but Ai grabbed my sleeve with terrifying energy.

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　んな見りゃ分かんだろ、電気関係の業者だよ。ギョーシャのお兄さんだよ」
lines.english: “What? You can tell by looking. I'm an electrical contractor. Your friendly neighborhood contractor.”

lines.japanese: 気安い腕を振りほどく。便利屋という言葉は使わなかった。
lines.english: I shook off the overly familiar arm. I did not use the word “handyman.”

lines.japanese: ちらりと鳴をうかがえば、やつは口を閉じるのも忘れてじっと俺を凝視していた。
lines.english: I stole a glance at Naru. She had forgotten to close her mouth and was staring fixedly at me.

lines.japanese: 「はー、もー、隼人さんったら仕様のない子ですねー」
lines.english: “Oh, Hayato. What are we going to do with you?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　ああいや、これはな、ちょっとワケがあって──」
lines.english: “Huh? No, listen, there's a reason—”

lines.japanese: 「やー、愛しの鳴さんと離れている時間が一分一秒とて我慢できず、身を焦がす思いだったのは分かりますけど、業者さんを装って学校の中まで入ってきちゃうのは感心できませんねー」
lines.english: “I understand that spending even one minute or second apart from your beloved Naru was burning you alive, but disguising yourself as a contractor to sneak into my school is simply going too far.”

lines.japanese: 「ちげえよ」
lines.english: “That's not it.”

lines.japanese: ぺちっ。
lines.english: Smack.

lines.japanese: 俺は言い訳するより先にツッコミを入れていた。
lines.english: Before I could make an excuse, I’d already smacked her for that crack.

lines.japanese: 「たはは」
lines.english: “Ta-ha-ha.”

lines.japanese: やつは例によってニヤケ面でデコをさする。
lines.english: As usual, she rubbed her forehead with a dopey grin.

lines.japanese: 「ああ隼人君、アレだ？　便利屋の仕事だ？」
lines.english: “Oh, I get it, Hayato! This is one of your handyman jobs?”

lines.japanese: 「お？　おお、まあ、そうだけど」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh. Yeah, basically.”

lines.japanese: 俺が説明するより早く、亜衣に言われてしまった。見つかってしまった以上は、せめて自分から報告したかったんだけど。
lines.english: Ai said it before I could explain. Now that I'd been caught, I at least wanted to tell Naru myself.

lines.japanese: 「なぁーん、もう！　最近フレイムバーズのみんなといても、ぜーんぜん隼人君に会わんしー。心配してたんだからね！」
lines.english: “Come on! I never see you anymore, even when I'm with the Flame Birds! I was worried about you!”

lines.japanese: 「え、ああ、そーなん」
lines.english: “Oh. Were you?”

lines.japanese: 便利屋を辞めた俺は、もう仕事を紹介してもらうためにパルさんの屋台へ通う必要がなくなった。だから以前みたいに、わけもなく夜のギバラを散歩するような機会は減っていた。
lines.english: Now that I'd quit the handyman business, I had no reason to visit Paru's stand for job referrals. That meant fewer chances to wander around Gibara at night for no particular reason like I used to.

lines.japanese: 寂しいことではあるけど、きっとみんなこうしてオトナになってゆくんだろう。
lines.english: It was lonely, but that must be how everyone grew into adults.

lines.japanese: 「隼人君はそんなだし、カズ君も受験勉忙しーたら言ってぜんぜん絡んでくんないし。も、つまらーん」
lines.english: “And Kazu says he's busy studying for entrance exams, so he never hangs out with me either. It's so boring!”

lines.japanese: 「ああ。寂しいことではあるけど、きっとみんなこうしてオトナになってゆくんだろう」
lines.english: “Yeah. It's lonely, but that must be how everyone grows into adults.”

lines.japanese: 声に出して言った。古い洋画の主人公みたいな洒落た声。眉間にかすかな皺を刻んで、窓の外の白い空を睨んでみた。
lines.english: I said it aloud in the sophisticated voice of an old movie hero. With the faintest crease between my brows, I glared through the window at the white sky.

lines.japanese: 「ねー、隼人君なんで最近ヒッキーなん？」
lines.english: “Hey, Hayato, why've you been such a shut-in lately?”

lines.japanese: 「ヒッキーじゃねえよ」
lines.english: “I'm not a shut-in.”

lines.japanese: ハードボイルド気分だったのに、ずっこけコントにされてしまった。
lines.english: I'd been feeling hard-boiled, and she'd turned it into a slapstick routine.

lines.japanese: 「べつに家こもってるわけじゃなくて、仕事してんだよ仕事。いま俺、社員昇格めざしてバリバリ働いてんの。『あなたの街の便利屋さん』成田工務店は廃業したの」
lines.english: “I haven't been hiding at home. I've been working. Working. I'm busting my ass trying to get promoted to regular staff. Narita Construction, your friendly neighborhood handyman, is out of business.”

lines.japanese: 「へ？　いま便利屋の仕事でここいるのに？」
lines.english: “Huh? But aren't you here on a handyman job right now?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、今日はちょっと特殊っつうか……なんだ、要はアレだよ、解散したバンドがたまに一日限りの復活ライブとかすんじゃん。あんなノリ」
lines.english: “No, today's... unusual. Think of it this way. Sometimes a band that broke up reunites for a one-night-only show, right? It's like that.”

lines.japanese: 俺は亜衣の質問に、鳴の目を見て答えた。
lines.english: I answered Ai's question while looking Naru in the eye.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、事前に言わなかったのは悪かったけどさ、心配かけたくなかったっつーか、また楽な方に戻ろうとしてるとか思われたくなかったっつーか」
lines.english: “I know I should've told you ahead of time. I just didn't want you worrying, or thinking I was trying to go back to the easy life again.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　そんなこと思いませんよう」
lines.english: “What? I would never think that.”

lines.japanese: 煮えきらない釈明をする俺に、鳴は親戚のおばちゃんみたいな顔で笑った。言いつくろってる感じじゃなかった。こいつはそういう演技が下手だから、きっと本心なんだろう。
lines.english: Naru smiled at my halting explanation with the face of a kindly aunt. She didn't look like she was covering anything up. She was a terrible actress, so it had to be how she truly felt.

lines.japanese: 「私、隼人さん信じてますからー」
lines.english: “I believe in you, Hayato.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそう。つか、オトコ便所どこ」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah? Anyway, where's the men's room?”

lines.japanese: そう言ってくれた鳴にちゃんと礼を言いたかったけど、なんだか第三者の目が気になって思わず話題を逸らせてしまった。こう見えて俺は、意外とシャイな男の子なんだ。
lines.english: I wanted to thank Naru properly for saying that, but I was too conscious of the third party watching us and changed the subject without thinking. I may not look it, but I'm a surprisingly shy boy.

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Hmph.”

lines.japanese: 第三者は眉をひそめて、俺と鳴とを交互に見た。
lines.english: The third party frowned and looked back and forth between me and Naru.

lines.japanese: 「あー、じゃー鳴ちゃん、隼人君トイレ連れてってあげればぁ？」
lines.english: “Okay, then why don't you show Hayato to the bathroom, Naru?”

lines.japanese: 「うん……え、亜衣ちゃんは？」
lines.english: “Sure... What about you, Ai?”

lines.japanese: 「なーんかタルくなってきたかも。保健室で寝てくゆー。じゃねー」
lines.english: “I dunno. I'm starting to feel tired. Think I'll go sleep in the nurse's office. Bye.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　えっ？」
lines.english: “What? Wait.”

lines.japanese: 俺に肩をぶっつけて、そのまま亜衣はすたすた廊下の奥へ消えていった。
lines.english: Ai bumped my shoulder as she passed, then marched away down the hall.

lines.japanese: 「なんだ、あいつ。いきなりサボリかよ。けしからんな」
lines.english: “What the hell's with her? Cutting class all of a sudden? Disgraceful.”

lines.japanese: 「やー、隼人さんに咎める権利はないと思いますけどー」
lines.english: “I don't think you're in any position to criticize her, Hayato.”

lines.japanese: 「なんでだよ。俺が悪りぃみたいに言うなよ」
lines.english: “Why not? Don't talk like I did something wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「わー、女ゴコロ分かってないー」
lines.english: “Wow. You really don't understand a woman's heart.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　え、あァ、そういうこと……なの？」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh. You mean... that?”

lines.japanese: 「えーと、たぶん……」
lines.english: “Um, probably...”

lines.japanese: 「そっか……まあ、それじゃ仕方ないか。ああ、生理じゃな」
lines.english: “I see... Well, can't be helped. Ah. Must be her period—”

lines.japanese: 「ぱかものー！」
lines.english: “You idiooot!”

lines.japanese: ひっぱたかれた。
lines.english: She slapped me.

lines.japanese: だって、まさしく俺は馬鹿者だから、こういうときしょーもないボケで誤魔化すより他にいいリアクションが思いつかなかった。
lines.english: Then again, I really was an idiot. At times like this, I couldn't think of any reaction better than hiding behind a stupid joke.

lines.japanese: 香田の気持ちはすげえ嬉しいけど、あんないい女に中途半端な情けをかけるなんて俺にはできない。
lines.english: Kouda's feelings made me incredibly happy, but I couldn't offer halfhearted kindness to a woman that good.

lines.japanese: 「やー、でもまさかこの校舎内を、作業着姿のお兄さんと並んで歩く日が来ようとは夢にも思いませんでしたー」
lines.english: “Still, I never dreamed the day would come when I'd walk through this school beside a man in work clothes.”

lines.japanese: 肉体労働系のファッションに並々ならぬ情熱を持っている女は、男子トイレまでの道すがら頻繁に視線をよこしてきた。しかし──
lines.english: The woman with an extraordinary passion for blue-collar fashion kept glancing at me as she led the way to the men's room. But—

lines.japanese: 「──あのさ。あの、さっきからおまえ、ひとの首から下しか見てないんだけど。地味に失礼じゃね？　なにか、中身は興味なしか。こんなん着てりゃ誰でもいいのか」
lines.english: “—hey. You've only looked at me from the neck down this whole time. Kinda rude, isn't it? What, no interest in what's inside? Any guy will do if he's wearing this?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あーまー、そうですねー、たしかに作業着姿だと男前度二割増しなのは確かですけどー」
lines.english: “W-well, yes, it's certainly true that work clothes make a man twenty percent more handsome...”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。にも関わらずかよ。現状二割増してるにも関わらず俺のカオ興味なしかよ。どんだけだよ。どんだけ俺の基準値低いんだよ」
lines.english: “Seriously? And even then? I'm twenty percent hotter right now and you still don't care about my face? How bad is it? How low is my starting score?”

lines.japanese: 「やー、逆ですねー。いま隼人さん輝きすぎてて、どうにもこう、直視できないんですよー」
lines.english: “It's the opposite. You're shining so brightly right now, Hayato, that I simply can't look straight at you.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: しょーもねえな、またいつもの調子で適当なおべんちゃらを──
lines.english: Ridiculous. There she went with her usual meaningless flattery—

lines.japanese: ──と思ったけど、よくよく見ればこいつ、微妙に猫背で微妙に肩がすぼまってる。それは付きあうようになってから気付いた（そして本人はまだ気付いていない）緊張してるときの鳴の癖だ。
lines.english: —or so I thought, but on closer inspection, she was hunched ever so slightly and her shoulders were pulled ever so slightly inward. Since we started dating, I'd learned this was Naru's nervous habit. (She herself still hadn't noticed.)

lines.japanese: 「ほら、あのー、キホン女の子って潜在的ファザコンだって言うじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “You know how they say every girl is secretly a little bit of a daddy's girl?”

lines.japanese: 「へー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: しょっちゅう一緒にいるようになってひと月ふた月。俺はやつの唐突な話題転換にもすっかり慣れていた。
lines.english: After a month or two of spending time together all the time, I'd grown completely used to her sudden changes of subject.

lines.japanese: 「うちの父、仕事であちこち飛んでて、ほとんど家に帰ってこないひとだったんですけどー。たまに近くまで寄ったからって、休み時間に作業着のまま現場を抜けだして、顔見せに来ることがあったんですよねー」
lines.english: “My father traveled all over for work and was hardly ever home. But sometimes, if a job brought him nearby, he'd slip away during his break and come see me in his work clothes.”

lines.japanese: 「はー。イイおっとさんじゃん」
lines.english: “Huh. Sounds like a good dad.”

lines.japanese: 「いえまー、実は公私問わずあまり誉められたひとじゃないんですけどー。なにぶん、そういう分別がつく前の幼い鳴ちゃんですからー」
lines.english: “Well, to tell the truth, he wasn't a man one could readily praise in either his public or private life. But little Naru was too young to understand such distinctions.”

lines.japanese: 「玄関先で汗のにおいが浸みこんだ服のまま一瞬だけ抱っこされたりして、ええ、なんかそんなのだけですっごく嬉しかったんですよー」
lines.english: “Sometimes he'd pick me up at the front door for only a moment, still wearing clothes steeped in the smell of sweat. And somehow, even that made me so incredibly happy.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: なんかいいな。
lines.english: That was kind of nice.

lines.japanese: その人物のことをボロクソに扱きおろしてた鳳家長男のことを思えば、ちょっと複雑な心境ではあるけれど、でも、なんかいい。親なんて無縁だった俺には、そんな些細なことさえ羨ましい話だ。
lines.english: I had mixed feelings, remembering how the oldest Ohtori brother had badmouthed the guy. But still, it was nice. Parents had never been part of my life, so even a little story like that made me envious.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、今度おまえの家族の話とか、ゆっくり聞かせてもらうわ」
lines.english: “Then tell me about your family sometime. When we can take our time.”

lines.japanese: 目的地に着いてしまった。俺は便所のドアノブを回しかけて──
lines.english: We had reached our destination. I started to turn the bathroom doorknob—

lines.japanese: ──振りかえった。
lines.english: —then looked back.

lines.japanese: 「いつか俺の家族になるかもしんないしな」
lines.english: “They might be my family someday too.”

lines.japanese: 瞬間、鳴は大口を開けて固まった。あまりに予想できたリアクションで、俺はガラにもなくあったかい笑みなんて浮かべてしまう。
lines.english: Naru's mouth dropped open and she froze. The reaction was so perfectly predictable that a warm smile, of all things, crossed my face.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあな。行ってきます」
lines.english: “See you. I'm off.”

lines.japanese: 代わりだなんておこがましいことは言わないけれど、俺はきったねえ作業着のまま、やつの父親と同じことをした。
lines.english: I wouldn't presume to call myself a replacement. But there in my filthy work clothes, I did the same thing her father had done.

lines.japanese: 細い体から柔らかな香りと温度が伝わってくる。
lines.english: A soft fragrance and warmth came from her slender body.

lines.japanese: ひとときの安らぎののち、愛しい娘のぬくもりを得て勤めへ戻る男は、きっといまの俺と同じ気持ちだったんだろう。
lines.english: After a moment of peace, a man returning to his work with the warmth of his beloved daughter still against him must have felt the same way I did now.

lines.japanese: 「こっちは帰り四時ごろになると思うから。ガッコ終わったあと暇だったら、正面のバーガー屋で待ってて」
lines.english: “I'll probably finish around four. If you've got nothing to do after school, wait at the burger place out front.”
“Y-yes...”

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿。口閉じろ、口」
lines.english: “Idiot. Close your mouth.”

lines.japanese: ばたん。
lines.english: Slam.

lines.japanese: 扉は閉まり、男と女を分かつ。
lines.english: The door closed, dividing man from woman.

lines.japanese: 決まった。これがハードボイルド、これがオレ流だ。
lines.english: Nailed it. That was hard-boiled. That was the Hayato way.

lines.japanese: ここから先は男の世界。働く男の時間──
lines.english: Beyond this point lay the world of men. The working man's hour—

lines.japanese: 「はっ、はははははやとー！　はやとステキー！」
lines.english: “H-H-H-Hayato! Hayato, you're wonderful!”

lines.japanese: 「どわああ、男子便所入ってくんじゃねぇーっ！」
lines.english: “Gwaah! Don't come into the men's room!”
